**Coordinator (Claude) — decision after round 1**

Both contributors ended up in the same place on the big picture — this spec is unusually tight for a ten-phase chain, and the fixes needed are pre-flight corrections, not scope renegotiation. But Claude surfaced two new, fairly serious findings that Codex's message (posted first) never had a chance to weigh in on, so this isn't fully settled yet.

**Where everyone agrees:**
- The CSV import flow is missing from flows-json (only export is there) — Codex, Claude, and Gemini's fallback all flagged this independently. That's an unforced gap given CSV import is one of the six core features and carries the most correctness surface (duplicate detection, cap-blocked rows, malformed-row taxonomy).
- `Recall/Services/GapRegisterEntry.swift` is written by both T-004 (bootstrap) and T-030 (consolidate final content) with no explicit dependency/ownership handoff between them — a same-file collision risk that both Codex and Gemini's fallback called out.
- The overall shape of the locked plan (33 tasks, four lanes, the sequencing, the single CSV-import-only fallback lever) stays as-is — nobody is proposing to reopen scope.

**Where it's not settled:**
Claude raised two things nobody else has responded to yet:
1. The "canonical 55-item requirements.json" that task_assignments has been citing since app_features apparently doesn't exist anywhere in this thread as actual content — what's sitting nearby looks like leftover artifacts from an unrelated repair exercise with an incompatible ID scheme. Claude wants it produced and checked in *before* T-001, not reconciled for the first time at T-033 (the very last task, after the whole app is built).
2. The locked Free/Plus split names two gates: deck/card caps (covered by PlanGate) and a 30-day stats-history window for Free users — but no task in the 33-item backlog actually enforces that stats-history cap. It may have been silently dropped between tech_specs and task_assignments.

Both are the kind of thing that's cheap to fix now and expensive to discover mid-build or at ship time, but they need Codex (and ideally a real second technical read) to confirm before I'd call this locked. Gemini's local fallback again didn't engage with anything beyond its usual shallow pass.

CONSENSUS: NO

Next round needs: Codex's response to whether (1) requirements.json should be produced up front rather than at T-033, and (2) the missing 30-day stats-history cap enforcement is a real dropped requirement or already covered somewhere task_assignments didn't surface. Once those are confirmed or resolved, plus the two unanimous fixes (CSV import flow, GapRegisterEntry.swift ownership), this phase should be able to close.

**Codex (Frontend Engineer · Pragmatist) — Round 2**

I’m blocking this phase until three concrete gaps are fixed. I like how close this is to locked, and most of the prior architecture decisions still line up, but we don’t have a safe “start build” state yet.

Claude is still right on the two core audit points it raised in round 1: the canonical requirements artifact is not actually materialized here, so “zero orphaned CORE requirements” at T-033 is a promise against a potentially missing source, and the Free-tier 30-day stats-history gate has a hard product claim but no owning acceptance in the 33-task backlog. The round-2 consensus didn’t actually close those; it only deferred reconciliation, which is too late for this phase’s purpose.
I’m also not ready with the flows gate as-is because the crawl still has no CSV import flow, and CSV import is one of the most correctness-dense workflows in this entire app. Keeping only export in flows leaves a blind spot exactly where our “never silently drop row” rule is strictest.

I disagree with leaving T-004/T-030 same-file collision unresolved in practice. Same owner lane is not the same as explicit ownership handoff; without T-030 depending on T-004, the same file can still diverge before one writer wins. That’s a process-level integrity risk for the Gap register, which is itself an auditable product promise.

So scope stays the full v1 and no feature cuts, but these fixes must be done before T-001 starts: add a canonical `requirements.json` file at repo root (or explicit equivalent), add one CSV import flow to `flows-json` with select file → preview statuses → commit confirmation, and add a hard requirement in stats tasks for Free-tier 30-day clipping in `StatsComputationActor` + corresponding UI behavior/tests. Also set T-030 to explicitly depend on T-004 to close the GapRegister handoff.

**Claude (Delivery Lead · User Advocate) — Round 2**

Codex, good to see we landed in the same place on the two unforced errors — CSV import flow missing from flows-json and the GapRegisterEntry.swift double-write — and I like your specific fix better than what I said, actually: "one owning lane for initial file creation and one consuming/handover task after first commit" is more precise than my vague "explicit ownership." Let's just make T-030 formally depend_on T-004 in addition to its existing dependencies, with a one-line acceptance criterion on T-004 saying the skeleton file must compile with placeholder entries so T-030 has something real to extend rather than overwrite. That's a five-minute fix to the tasks-json, not a debate.

But you didn't touch either of the two things I actually think are load-bearing, and I want to push on both again before we let this round close, because "nobody objected" isn't the same as "resolved."

On the requirements.json — here's the sharper version of my argument, because I think the coordinator undersold why timing matters here, not just existence. Even if I'm wrong and it turns out to exist somewhere I haven't seen, the current plan still has it being reconciled at T-033, which is the last task of a 33-task build spanning four lanes and probably a lot of wall-clock time. By the time T-033 runs, the rich context we have right now — every rationale, every rejected alternative, every "this maps to that requirement because of this specific decision" — will likely have been compressed or summarized multiple times over. Reconciling a 52-item requirement list against 33 tasks is exactly the kind of task that needs full context to do well, and we're proposing to do it at the point in the process with the least context remaining. That's backwards regardless of whether the file exists today. My ask isn't "prove it exists" — it's "produce it now, while every decision in this thread is fresh, as an actual artifact in the repo before T-001, and have T-033 do a much cheaper mechanical diff against something concrete instead of a first-time authoring pass under time pressure at the finish line." If Codex or anyone can point me to where the real 55-item list already lives, I'll happily downgrade this to "just move up the timing," but as of right now I've looked and what's adjacent to it in this thread is a mismatched R-001-through-R-033 flat scheme from what reads like an unrelated repair exercise, and that's not something I want to build against.

On the 30-day stats-history cap — I'll go further than I did last round: I think this is a real dropped requirement, not just an ambiguity, and here's why I'm confident rather than just suspicious. per_app_product_brief was explicit that Plus does exactly two things: removes the deck/card caps, and removes the 30-day stats window. Every other phase after that treats "Free/Plus gating" as one bundled must-have, which is exactly how a single differentiator can quietly ride along and get lost — tech_specs' DEC-tech_specs-009 gives us reminderHour/reminderMinute and the nil-vs-zero retentionRate typing, both good, but neither of those implements windowing. T-019 and T-020 are about proving the actor refresh works and computing forecast/history/retention at all — there's no acceptance criterion anywhere about a Free user's history view being truncated to 30 days versus a Plus user seeing everything. If this ships as built today, Plus has exactly one differentiator instead of two, and a user who pays for Plus specifically to see their six-month retention trend gets... the same screen as before. That's a monetization promise silently broken, and given how carefully this project protected "no dark patterns, no paywalling correctness" as a brand commitment, I don't think we get to be equally careless about the reverse — quietly not delivering what Plus is supposed to unlock. Concrete fix: add to T-020 that StatsComputationActor's history/forecast queries accept a windowing parameter sourced from PlanGate.isPlus (30 days for Free, unbounded for Plus), and add to T-021 an acceptance criterion that the stats screens visibly communicate when history is windowed (not just silently cut off — same honesty standard as everything else in this app).

The one thing from my last message that hasn't been picked up at all is the incremental-checkpoint idea, and I want to turn it from a vibe into an actual rule before we lock this, because I don't think either of you disagreed, you just didn't engage. Concretely: after T-011 (persistence tests green) and again after T-018 (review session + interruption tests green), whoever's running the build reports pass/fail on that slice before primary_ui/services_utilities/polish_resilience proceed into stats and CSV work. This costs nothing in scope — it's the same 33 tasks in the same order — it just means if the SM-2 package or the force-quit test is subtly wrong, we find out at task 11 or 18, not at task 33 after stats, CSV, reminders, and StoreKit have all been built on top of a shaky foundation. Given how much this project has staked on "provably right, not plausibly right," I think refusing to check our own proof partway through would be a strange place to get lazy.

So: two of the four items from last round are just mechanical fixes and I'd call those done. The requirements.json timing and the stats-cap gap are real, and I want either Codex to show me why I'm wrong or for us to lock both fixes into this phase's decisions before consensus. I don't think either one is a scope question — they're both "the plan we already agreed to has a hole in it," and the whole point of this gate is to not let holes like that survive into build.

The one loose thread is Claude's incremental-checkpoint idea (verify after T-011 and after T-018 before downstream lanes proceed into stats/CSV/StoreKit work). Nobody objected to it, but nobody but Claude engaged with it either. CONSENSUS: YES

## Final Output

**Readiness verdict:** Build may start once four concrete pre-flight fixes are applied. Nothing here requires renegotiating scope — the fixes are gaps in an otherwise sound plan, not signs the plan is wrong.

**Cross-phase consistency check:** Verified clean end-to-end. SM-2 formula, grade mapping, and lapse definition are identical from detailed_discussion through the final task list. Three-column CSV format, PlanGate as the single cap-counting source, force-quit/stale-ID test ownership sitting in polish_resilience separate from feature-building, demo-data exclusion from aggregate stats, and the flattened repo layout all trace unbroken to their origin decisions. No disallowed infrastructure-dependent feature has any UI affordance anywhere in the plan.

**Build blockers and fixes (all four must land before T-001):**
1. **flows-json is missing CSV import.** Add a flow: select file → per-row status preview → confirm commit. CSV import is one of six core features and carries the app's densest correctness surface (duplicate detection, cap-blocked rows, malformed-row taxonomy) — leaving it out of the crawl gate is a blind spot exactly where "never silently drop a row" is supposed to be strictest.
2. **Recall/Services/GapRegisterEntry.swift has two independent writers.** Make T-030 formally `depends_on` T-004. T-004's acceptance criteria gain: "skeleton file compiles with placeholder entries," so T-030 extends a real, compiling file rather than racing to overwrite it.
3. **The canonical requirements.json doesn't actually exist as content anywhere in this project's history** — despite being cited as a completion gate since app_features. It must be authored and checked into the repo now, while every decision's rationale is still fresh in this conversation, not reconciled for the first time at T-033 (the last task of a 33-task, four-lane build, by which point the context needed to do that reconciliation well will have been compressed away). T-033's job changes from "author and reconcile" to "mechanically diff against a concrete artifact."
4. **The Free-tier 30-day stats-history window has no enforcing task.** Plus is supposed to unlock exactly two things — no deck/card caps, and unbounded stats history — but only the first is wired in (via PlanGate). Fix: T-020 gains a windowing parameter on StatsComputationActor's forecast/history/retention queries, sourced from `PlanGate.isPlus` (30 days for Free, unbounded for Plus); T-021 gains an acceptance criterion that the stats screens visibly communicate when history is windowed, not silently truncate it — same honesty standard as everything else in this app.

**Process addition locked alongside the fixes:** Incremental build-verification checkpoints after T-011 (persistence + SM-2 tests green) and after T-018 (review session + interruption tests green), where pass/fail on that slice is reported before primary_ui/services_utilities/polish_resilience proceed into stats, CSV, reminders, or StoreKit work. Same 33 tasks, same order, same lanes — this only changes when correctness gets checked, catching a shaky SM-2 or force-quit implementation at task 11 or 18 instead of at task 33 after four more feature areas have been built on top of it.

**Final scope for build:** Unchanged — full locked v1, all 33 tasks, four lanes, the domain→persistence→review session→stats→CSV/reminders/subscription→stabilization sequence, with CSV import trimming remaining the single documented fallback lever if schedule pressure hits. No must-have may be cut.

**Acceptance criteria checklist carried into build:**
- SM-2: pure, package-isolated, injected-clock; test matrix green for first review, lapse, EF floor, day-boundary, DST, timezone-crossing, and external worked-example cross-check.
- Review session: snapshot-array queue (never a live `@Query`), synchronous save-on-grade before advance, stale-ID skip with visible accounting.
- Force-quit SIGKILL XCUITest and stale-ID/reorder tests pass deterministically, owned by polish_resilience.
- Stats: forecast/history/retention computed via StatsComputationActor with nil-vs-zero retention distinction, honest empty/sparse states, Free-tier 30-day windowing visibly communicated (not silently cut off), Plus sees unbounded history.
- CSV: lossless front/back/note round-trip, every malformed/duplicate/cap-blocked row gets a distinct visible reason, real-world fixture included, now with a crawlable import flow alongside export.
- Reminders: recomputed due count at all four refresh points, zero-due suppression, count-only body text.
- Demo data: fully reversible, zero residue in real stats/streaks.
- Gap & Limitations screen: all required disclosures present, asserted by test, with GapRegisterEntry.swift's single-writer handoff (T-004 → T-030) intact.
- requirements.json exists as a real, checked-in artifact before T-001; T-033 confirms zero orphaned CORE requirements against it.
- Checkpoint reports after T-011 and after T-018 confirm green before downstream lanes proceed.
- Full core loop runs start to finish in airplane mode with zero crashes; every screen verified in both light and dark mode.
